source.title: AdaFisher: Adaptive Second Order Optimization via Fisher Information
source.authors: Damien Martins Gomes; Yanlei Zhang; Eugene Belilovsky; Guy Wolf; Mahdi S. Hosseini

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present; some table values are flattened, but the reported accuracy values used below can be assigned to their rows.
record.tranche_reason: Compares held-out performance across optimizers, bearing conceptually on V4, though its main subject is the new AdaFisher optimizer.
record.gate_note: Results on CIFAR and language benchmarks compare optimizer test accuracy or perplexity. The paper does not test memorization of random labels, width past interpolation, convolutional versus fully connected architectures, dropout, sharpness-gap ranking, or removal of memorized examples. Optimizer hyperparameter selection details are setup, not separate results.
record.test_reason: The study independently compares Adam/AdamW with momentum SGD on held-out image accuracy, bearing on V4. Its distributed ImageNet experiment also measures batch-size effects at a fixed 90 epochs, bearing on V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: they claim AdaFisher improves accuracy, convergence speed, stability, and tuning robustness across tested image and language tasks. Their superiority claim has exceptions: at equal 200 epochs, Shampoo slightly exceeds AdaFisher on ResNet18 CIFAR100, 77.35% versus 77.28%, while taking substantially longer.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces AdaFisher, a diagonal block-Kronecker Fisher preconditioner, and compares it with SGD, Adam/AdamW, and other optimizers; uses its own tuning and wall-clock training cutoffs.
record.method_sensitivity: Test accuracy varies by dataset, architecture, optimizer, and training cutoff; AdaFisher's reported accuracy is also evaluated across batch sizes and learning rates, but the stability figures do not provide extractable numerical values in the supplied text.

fits_no_version.finding: AdaFisher/AdaFisherW outperform the selected optimizer baselines in the extracted image and language comparisons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed Fisher-based optimizer improves held-out performance under the study's training and tuning budgets.

fits_no_version.finding: AdaFisher produces narrower, smaller FIM-diagonal distributions than Adam, interpreted by the authors as evidence of flatter minima.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: FIM-diagonal distributions differ between these optimizers during training; this does not establish magnitude-aware sharpness ranking generalization gaps.

record.problems: Optimizer comparisons use wall-clock cutoffs based on AdaFisher training epochs, so epoch counts differ by optimizer. CIFAR results average five runs; Tiny ImageNet and ImageNet-1k use one trial each. The study does not test random-label memorization or measure train-test gaps directly.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows from the optimizer comparison tables were extracted; selected rows cover representative matched model and dataset comparisons bearing on V4. The paper also reports many other architectures and optimizer pairs in Tables 2–5 and 12–15.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and corresponding held-out performance versus natural-label training.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local-connectivity explanations.

The exact learning-rate-and-schedule-only tuning restriction; effects of expanding tuning, switching from Adam to SGD, or isolating decoupled weight decay; adaptive-versus-SGD language-model performance. Training-performance equivalence cannot be established from the supplied figure captions.

The workload-dependent failure threshold, batches beyond 1024 in the study's own ImageNet experiments, language-model batch effects, and controlled interventions isolating longer training, warmup, normalization, or regularization.
Dropout interventions and interactions with training-set size, augmentation, or weight decay.
Magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation tolerance, its ranking of generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm or margin measures.
Removal of memorized examples versus equally sized random removals.

missing.what: Matched AdamW-versus-SGD rows for vision transformers, needed to represent the architecture-dependent reversal. Other table comparisons are broadly declared omitted, but the selected rows omit this verdict-relevant condition group.

Fixed-90-epoch batch comparison: AdaFisher ResNet50 ImageNet-1k top-1 accuracy 76.95, 77.01, and 77.09 at batch sizes 256, 512, and 1024. This V5 experiment is absent from both the rows and the declared table omissions.
missing.locator: Table 3; Figure 15; Appendix A.4 and D.2.4

record.verdict_notes: The blanket extracted V4 verdict is inappropriate: CNN Adam-versus-SGD results support the reported ordering, transformer results qualify its scope, and adaptive-versus-adaptive language comparisons cannot establish it. Batch-size stability curves in Figures 6 and 23 lack readable values and an explicit fixed-epoch budget in the supplied text. Literature-derived ImageNet baselines in Table 3 are not this study's results.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error as width grows beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.

The study compares AdaFisher and AdaFisherW with several optimizers on image and language tasks, but does not test Wilson et al.'s specific adaptive-method comparison under limited tuning, or the stated effects of broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, or switching from Adam to SGD.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations to the recipe.
Dropout effects and interactions with augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness as a predictor of train-test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy changes.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SGD; reports test accuracy after the study's CIFAR training cutoff.
rows.note: Optimizer comparison; the table reports performance but this row alone does not establish an adaptive-versus-SGD effect.
rows.check: Valid SGD control for R2. Add Cutout augmentation and the actual 226 training epochs; the cutoff is wall-clock time equivalent to 200 AdaFisher epochs.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Adam; reports test accuracy after the study's CIFAR training cutoff.
rows.check: Use R1 as baseline: Adam accuracy is 94.85±0.1 versus SGD's 95.64±0.1. Add Cutout and the actual 210 Adam epochs. The recipe also tunes SGD momentum, so it does not reproduce learning-rate-and-schedule-only tuning.

rows.subject: ResNet18

relationships.condition: ResNet18 trained from scratch on CIFAR10 and CIFAR100 with Cutout, batch 256, matched wall-clock budgets
relationships.reason: R2 versus R1 and R5 versus R4 show Adam accuracy lower by 0.79 and 0.82 percentage points. This supports the optimizer ordering under this recipe; SGD momentum tuning and unequal epoch counts qualify its correspondence to limited tuning.
relationships.display_finding: Reported Adam accuracy trails SGD by 0.79 and 0.82 points, but verification remains incomplete and momentum tuning and unequal training durations complicate interpretation.

relationships.condition: CIFAR vision transformers: Tiny Swin, FocalNet, and CCT-2/3×2
relationships.reason: Based on Table 2 text, without corresponding extracted rows: AdamW exceeds SGD on both datasets for all three architectures; for Tiny Swin, accuracies are 87.37 versus 82.34 and 60.21 versus 54.89. The ordering depends on architecture and recipe.
relationships.display_finding: AdamW reportedly exceeded SGD across all three architectures on both datasets, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: Distributed AdaFisher, ResNet50 on ImageNet-1k, 90 epochs, batches 256–1024
relationships.reason: Based on Table 3 and Figure 15's caption, without extracted rows: top-1 accuracy is 76.95%, 77.01%, and 77.09% at batches 256, 512, and 1024. This recipe shows no numerical penalty over that tested range; no uncertainty is reported.
relationships.display_finding: Small top-1 accuracy increases across the batch sweep were reported without uncertainty, but these comparisons remain unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.condition: ResNet18 on CIFAR10 and CIFAR100; scaled-down GPT-1 on WikiText-2
reader_labels.reason: AdaFisher/AdaFisherW outperform the listed SGD and Adam/AdamW comparators in these reported conditions (R1–R8), so this study does not show that adaptive methods necessarily generalize worse; it tests a different adaptive optimizer and recipe.
